text:
A. Exam creation and editing (Doraemon)

1. Editing an exam changes the answer key.
Doraemon imports an SSC paper where Q5 has 5 options and the correct answer is option 5. He fixes a typo in the title and clicks Save Changes. The edit form only has 4 option boxes, so option 5 disappears. No radio is selected for the missing option, so the correct answer is saved as option 1. Nobitha answers correctly and is marked wrong. Nobody sees an error.

2. Blank options appear in the exam.
Doraemon types a question with only options A and B and leaves C and D empty. The exam shows Nobitha two empty choices. If Doraemon left the correct-answer radio on the empty C, the answer key is “nothing”.

3. Image-option questions can’t be answered.
Doraemon imports a reasoning paper where the four options are pictures. The preview shows the pictures. Nobitha’s exam shows https://…png text as the options, so he can’t tell which is which. The results page does the same.

4. Telugu and Hindi exams may refuse to save.
Doraemon creates a 300-question Telugu exam. The app measures size in characters and thinks it fits. Firestore counts bytes, and Telugu uses 3 bytes per character, so the real size is over 1 MB. The save fails with a confusing error.

5. “Generate from Notes” can get stuck.
Nobitha pastes notes and clicks Generate. The AI returns one question with no options list. The app crashes while drawing the preview and the Generate button stays greyed out. He has to close the whole popup and start over.

6. “Send to Student” lies.
Doraemon opens a result and clicks “Send to Student”. A popup says “Report has been sent to student’s email”. Nothing was sent. “Download Report” also does nothing.

7. The Create Exam form can close while he types.
Nobitha tried to open an exam that hadn’t started and saw a countdown popup. He clicked OK, but the countdown kept running in the background. A few minutes later it ran closeDynamicModal() and closed whatever was open. If he was in the middle of typing a Create Exam form, the form vanishes.

B. Starting an exam (Nobitha)

8. Pressing Esc breaks the exam start.
Nobitha clicks Take Exam and sees the agreement popup, or “camera problem – ask examiner”. He presses Esc or clicks outside the popup. The popup closes, but the app is still waiting for a button click that will never come. His camera light stays on. If Doraemon later approves the camera request, the exam starts by itself.

9. “I Fixed It — Retry” does nothing.
Nobitha’s browser blocked the camera. He fixes it and clicks Retry. The app treats Retry as Cancel and closes everything. He has to click Take Exam again.

10. A working camera is rejected because the mic is missing.
Nobitha’s laptop has a camera but the mic is disabled. The app asks for camera and mic in one request, so the whole request fails. It says “camera unavailable” even though the camera works.

11. A dim room counts as a covered camera.
Nobitha is in a dim room, or the webcam is slow to adjust its brightness. The app checks two frames in the first second, sees dark, and says “camera blocked”. He has to ask Doraemon for approval.

12. He stays stuck in fullscreen.
Nobitha clicks Take Exam. The questions fail to load because of bad internet. The app goes back to the dashboard but never leaves fullscreen.

13. The exam is killed by mistake.
Nobitha clicks Take Exam. While the questions load from GitHub (a few seconds), Doraemon happens to fix a typo in that exam. The app sees “scheduled” from the server, thinks Doraemon cancelled the exam, and shows “Exam Re-assigned”.

C. During the exam (Nobitha)

14. Clicking anywhere outside the window submits the exam instantly.
Nobitha has a second monitor and clicks on it by accident. The exam submits at once. By contrast, leaving fullscreen gives him a 10-second warning, so the two rules are inconsistent.

15. The timer is red from the start of the second exam.
Nobitha finishes one exam with under a minute left, so the timer turned red. He starts another exam without refreshing. The timer is already red and pulsing, because the colour class was never removed.

16. The clock resets after a crash.
Nobitha’s laptop dies 30 minutes into a 60-minute exam. When he reopens the app, the live-status record is missing for some reason. The app then gives him the full 60 minutes again.

17. After “continue without camera” approval, the red screen comes back.
Nobitha’s camera shutter is closed. Doraemon approves continuing without camera. When the camera reports “muted” again, the blocked screen reappears even though Doraemon already approved.

18. Cheating by freezing the clock.
The timer pauses when the camera is blocked or the internet is off. A student could cover the camera, think for ten minutes, and uncover it. The time only freezes. It isn’t lost.

19. A section is skipped.
Section 1’s time runs out and a “Time’s up” screen shows for 1.4 seconds. If Nobitha clicks Submit Section in that gap, the app moves him to Section 2 and then to Section 3. Section 2 is locked and he can’t go back.

20. The Back button needs many presses after the exam.
After the exam, Nobitha presses Back to leave the site. Nothing happens, because the app added extra history entries to block Back during the exam. He needs several presses.

21. Answer keys travel to the student’s browser.
The question list, including the correct answers, is downloaded to Nobitha’s browser. Anyone who opens developer tools can read the answers.

22. Live video fails on some networks.
Doraemon clicks Watch Live from a corporate or strict network and sees a black screen. The app only has a STUN server and no TURN server, so some networks can’t connect.

D. Scoring and results

23. Typing nonsense earns marks.
A short-answer question has no expected answer set. Nobitha types “asdfghjklzzz” (more than 10 characters). The app counts it correct and gives 70% of the marks.

24. The same attempt can score differently.
If saving to the server fails, the app grades locally and rounds the 70% down. The server rounds it to the nearest whole mark. The same answers can score differently depending on which path ran.

25. A failed notification wipes the real result.
Nobitha submits. Everything saves, but the notification to Doraemon fails. The app thinks the whole submit failed, grades locally, and overwrites the real result.

26. “Latest score” and “Improvement trend” can be wrong.
The dashboard takes the last exam in the list, not the most recent by date. After he took a new exam, the dashboard might still show an older one as “latest”.

27. Results can crash.
If the question list changed after grading, opening the results page crashes. Old exams missing idle-time data can show “NaN”.

E. Dashboard and calendar

28. Typing in search gets slower over time.
Each time the dashboard refreshes (and that happens on every database change), the app adds another search listener. After 20 refreshes, one keystroke runs the search 20 times.

29. The page jumps to the top.
Nobitha is scrolled halfway down his Results tab. Doraemon schedules another exam. The page jumps to the top.

30. The calendar throws him back to the month view.
Nobitha is viewing the 25th with three to-dos. Doraemon ticks one off. Nobitha is thrown back to the month view.

31. A simultaneous tick-off loses one.
Nobitha and Doraemon both tick the same to-do in the same second. Only one tick is kept.

32. Clicking Allow opens an unrelated popup.
Nobitha’s examiner clicks Allow on the “waiting for approval” card on the dashboard. The Notifications window pops open. The card in the bell menu also still shows Allow/Deny, as if unanswered.

33. Dozens of notifications on every login.
Doraemon has 200 old notifications. When he logs in, he gets about 150 desktop notifications and popups for old events.

F. Notes (sticky notes)

34. A deleted-then-undone note disappears later.
Nobitha deletes a note, then clicks Undo within 5 seconds. During those 5 seconds any save also wrote _deleting: true into the file. After he refreshes, that note is hidden forever.

35. Two tabs overwrite each other.
Nobitha edits notes on his phone and on his laptop. The one that saves last wins. The other device’s changes vanish.

G. Books, translation and voice

36. “Open in this tab” stops working after translating.
Nobitha opens a PDF, picks Telugu, then clicks “Original PDF”. The “Open in this tab” button is dead and a loading spinner can stay on screen.

37. Deleting one exam breaks another exam’s images.
Doraemon imports the same paper twice, so both exams reuse one image file on GitHub. He deletes the first exam. The app also deletes the image file, so the second exam’s pictures turn into broken icons.

38. Deleting a base64-image exam is very slow.
Images were saved as base64 text because GitHub wasn’t set up. Deleting the exam sends giant, invalid requests five times per image. It is slow and fails.

39. Photos may be saved to GitHub.
Doraemon clicks “Capture Photo” during live proctoring. The popup says “Saved to GitHub”. It may actually have saved a big base64 copy into the exam record. It breaks the 1 MB limit after a few photos and the failure is hidden. If GitHub is configured, the student’s photo goes to your repo, which could be public.

H. Messages and settings

40. Telegram messages fail for some titles.
Doraemon names an exam “Maths < Physics” or “R&D Quiz”. Telegram can’t read the HTML and rejects the message. He never gets the alert.

41. Dark mode looks broken on a light-OS laptop.
Nobitha’s laptop is in light mode. He clicks the dark theme button. The grey text and borders disappear because the colour variables they use are only defined for OS dark mode.

42. The app doesn’t start with storage disabled.
Nobitha uses Chrome with “block all cookies and site data”. The theme setup throws an error on load and nothing works. It shows a blank login.

43. Login does nothing on plain http://.
Doraemon opens the app from a local-network address over http://. The browser’s crypto API is missing there. Clicking Login does nothing.

44. Popups disappear early.
Two popups appear 3 seconds apart. The second one is hidden at second 5 by the first one’s timer.

45. A to-do completion email goes to the wrong person.
When Nobitha completes a to-do, the “completion email” is addressed to himself, not to Doraemon who created it.

I. Security issues (every user)

46. Secrets are visible to anyone. The Telegram bot token, the Gemini key and the password hashes are in the JavaScript files. The GitHub token and Telegram token are also stored readable in Firestore. If the database rules are “test mode”, anyone who opens the site’s source can use your Gemini quota, spam your Telegram bot, or write to your GitHub repo. Please rotate those secrets.

47. Login is only a show. Nobitha opens developer tools and sets his saved username to doraemon. He is now the teacher. The “Delete All Data” button is protected by a client-side check, which he can also bypass. Only strict Firestore rules prevent that.

48. Script injection. Doraemon saves feedback containing </textarea>. The feedback box breaks, and text after it runs as HTML. A tampered notes file or pasted exam JSON can do the same through unescaped fields (note colour, image option URLs, settings fields).

J. Smaller issues
Stale cache after updating: only ui.js and notes.js have ?v= version tags. Browsers may keep the old exam-taking.js after you deploy.
Chart.js has no version or integrity check: a future Chart.js release could break the charts without warning.
Dead and duplicate code: deleteAllData, watchLiveExam, loadUserNotes, startProctoringBroadcast and _startIdleTracking are each defined twice. The earlier copies never run, but they confuse anyone editing the file.
Hindi books listed as English: two Home Science books (lehh1, lehh2) appear in the English list. I couldn’t verify this against NCERT’s list.
Orphaned data: deleting an exam leaves old GitHub chunk files and live-proctoring records behind.
Heavy data load: every login downloads every exam’s full question bank, and does so again on any change. It is slow with large exams.
